purpose: Teach: 慰霊/機関車/時効/パトカー/系譜/恐慌/靖国神社/内蔵

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、戦争、本気for、絶対、慰霊、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、感心
lines.en: Ren, your paper on war memorials was really thoughtful. I was genuinely impressed.
lines.style: Warm, steady observation. Lean forward slightly. Voice rises with genuine recognition on 'impressed.' No hurry—these words matter and you're saying them to someone who deserves to hear them.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。明治時代の、本気で、絶対、機関車、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you so much. The Meiji-era locomotive research was something I really wanted to do justice to. I appreciate you noticing.
lines.style: Genuine gratitude, slightly self-conscious. Quiet, steady pace. Eyes down briefly—not shame, just the vulnerability of being seen. Voice catches faintly on 'appreciate,' like the recognition matters more than he expected.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 刑法の、本気で、絶対、時効、絶対、制度、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、視野、広い、絶対、立派、絶対、本気で、感心
lines.en: And your work on criminal law—the statute of limitations—showed real breadth of thinking. That's the kind of work that stays with you.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost quietly moved. Slight pause before 'statute of limitations,' as if recalling something specific. Gentle emphasis on 'breadth.' Voice settles deeper, more introspective. Speaking not just to praise but to acknowledge something rare.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。警察の、本気で、絶対、パトカー、絶対、配備、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes. The research on police patrol car deployment—that took longer than I expected, but it felt important to get it right. Thank you for recognizing that.
lines.style: Measured, slightly earnest. Voice steady but with underlying relief—like someone who worried their effort might go unnoticed. Small breath before thanking her. Forward momentum, not rushed. Authentic gratitude without overstatement.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 各家系の、本気で、絶対、系譜、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: Your family genealogy research was meticulous. That kind of detail-work takes patience.
lines.style: Nod slightly. Warm recognition with no sentimentality. Voice clear, direct. A beat of acknowledgment before moving on—she's genuinely marking this as significant. Not effusive, but thorough in her attention.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。世界、本気で、絶対、恐慌、絶対、史、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes. The economic history—the Great Depression—that required pulling together so many different sources. I'm grateful you see the work that went into it.
lines.style: Quiet determination underneath. Voice steady and direct, not defensive. Small acknowledgment of effort without self-pity. Speaking as someone who knows they did solid work and is relieved an adult confirmed it. No waver, just honest thanks.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 本気で、絶対、靖国神社、絶対、史、絶対、論文で、絶対、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: Your Yasukuni Shrine historical analysis—that required real care and nuance. You handled it with integrity.
lines.style: Slower opening. Slight breath before naming the shrine, as if marking the weight of the subject. Voice lowers fractionally, more gravitas. Clear-eyed, serious. This is not casual praise—it's an adult acknowledging a young person's ethical seriousness on a difficult topic.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。日本の、本気で、絶対、内蔵、絶対、技術、絶対、史、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes. Japan's internal machinery and engineering history—I wanted to trace how those systems came together. Thank you for taking the time to really look at what I did.
lines.style: Solid, grounded. Voice carries quiet pride without arrogance. Speaking clearly, like someone who's done work they stand behind. Final thanks is warm and direct—not trailing off, but arriving at a quiet moment of genuine exchange. Pace is unhurried, as if this conversation is enough.
